article.articleTextExcerpt: The Municipal Corporation (MC) has terminated the three-year mechanical sweeping contract awarded to Karnal-based private firm Akanksha Enterprises, flagging major lapses. The project costed Rs 11.76 crore. Confirming this to The Tribune, MC Commissioner Pooja Syal Grewal said the company failed to meet prescribed coverage targets and violated operational norms. It also failed to provide quality machines according to laid down specifications and fell short of the manpower required to meet targets. An internal review based on GPS tracking revealed that the firm was covering less than 20 per cent of the targeted road length of 910 kilometres. The calculation of road length is based on a 10-foot width and the coverage capacity of a mechanical sweeping machine. If a road’s width is 20 feet, the length doubles, as a single machine covers a width of 10 feet. Internal findings indicated that the machines were required to operate at speeds of at least 8 km per hour for effective dust collection, but GPS records showed they were operating at lower speeds. article.postedBy: Metro, RRTS & High-Speed Rail Project Updates

article.articleTextExcerpt: A monorail runs on a single elevated beam rather than a conventional two-rail track. That makes it a compact, fully elevated mode, useful on dense urban corridors where road space is tight. In India the flagship is the Mumbai Monorail, the country’s first and so far only system. This page covers monorail in India: how the technology works, where it runs, and the latest developments. A monorail vehicle straddles or hangs from a single guideway beam, usually on rubber tyres. The result is a small footprint, a tight turning radius and a quiet ride. Most modern systems, Mumbai’s included, use the straddle-beam design, where the train sits astride a slim concrete beam. On capacity it sits below metro. It works well as a feeder or on medium-demand corridors, but it cannot match a metro’s throughput, which is why cities weigh it carefully against light metro and Metrolite. article.articleTextExcerpt: Assam to Get India’s First Underwater Road-Cum-Rail Tunnel Under Brahmaputra Assam’s ₹18,662-crore Gohpur-Numaligarh corridor includes India’s first underwater road-cum-rail tunnel beneath the Brahmaputra River. The new link could also bring more attention to properties in Gohpur and surrounding areas as connectivity improves. Similarly, properties in Numaligarh may see greater interest over time, particularly from buyers tracking major road and rail infrastructure projects. article.description: The Union Government has launched India’s first Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) powered diesel electric multiple unit (DEMU) train with eight coaches from Sabarmati railway station...
article.articleTextExcerpt: The Union Government has launched India’s first Liquified Natural Gas (LNG) powered diesel electric multiple unit (DEMU) train with eight coaches from Sabarmati railway station to Mahesana Junction in Gujarat as part of its green initiatives on September 27, 2026. The train is based on a diesel-LNG dual fuel system for operating its driving power cars (DPCs) on both diesel and LNG. This system lets LNG to substitute for about 40 per cent of diesel usage and a full tank of LNG can operate for around 1,600 km. Moreover, two DPCs with each having 1,400 horsepower (hp) of capacity has been transformed to function using this dual fuel system with LNG tank attached to each for holding 2,200 litres of LNG. Besides, field trials for these two DPCs have also been conducted on over 2,000 km to check its reliability.

I was happy to have him with me, but underneath I was worried. What if I did not perform well? What if my anxiety spoiled the journey for him? But Bhopal slowly took my mind elsewhere. We reached Bhopal and the first thing we noticed was how clean and orderly the station was. There was a sweetness in the way people spoke and lived their lives. It made me slow down. Then came the food. Hot poha, jalebi, dhokla, Bhopali paan and Bhopali chai. Nothing extraordinary, perhaps, but sitting with my father, putting my worries aside and eating without thinking about the examination felt strangely comforting. We visited the Upper and Lower Lakes. During the chase, head constable Velmurugan reportedly climbed onto the roof of the moving SUV and held on as it continued at high speed. The pursuit stretched for around 40 kilometres. A sub-inspector following the vehicle on a motorcycle alerted the police control room and ambulance services while the chase was underway. article.articleTextExcerpt: A snake species known as the 'Sistan sand boa' has been scientifically recorded in India for the first time after researchers found three of them in Rajasthan's Sikar district. The Sistan sand boa (Eryx sistanensis) is a non-venomous, thick-bodied snake found in dry areas. It was earlier known to be from Iran and Pakistan. Researchers Vivek Sharma of Jabalpur and wildlife biologist Dharmendra Khandal of Ranthambhore-based Tiger Watch found three of these snakes during a survey in the Ramgarh-Shekhawati area of Sikar in 2025. Their study was published in the Journal of Threatened Taxa on May 26 this year. The first snake was found inside a gaushala on August 19, 2025. Another was found in the courtyard of a house at Sunda Ki Dhani on September 12 and the third near an under-construction house at Rukansar on September 21 last year. The researchers studied their body shape, colour and scales before identifying them as Sistan sand boas. "We knew that this snake was different, but we did not rush to publish a research paper. article.articleTextExcerpt: The Border Security Force (BSF) has recorded a sharp surge in narcotics recoveries along the Punjab frontier this year. More than 850 kg of heroin smuggled from Pakistan has been seized so far, more than double the 415 kg recovered in 2025 and nearly three times the 283 kg seized in 2024. Despite intensified counter-drone measures, unmanned aerial vehicles remained the preferred mode for cross-border smuggling. While 182 drones had been recovered till September-end this year, the figure stood at around 290 in each of the previous two years. Apart from heroin, the BSF seized around 14 kg of ICE (crystal methamphetamine) and 44 kg of opium. ICE recoveries remained largely at par with 2025, when 21 kg was seized, compared with just 1.4 kg in 2024. Opium seizures, meanwhile, rose from 12 kg last year and 16 kg in 2024 to 44 kg this year. Another notable trend has been the steady rise in the trafficking of sophisticated weapons by cross-border networks.
